clue.text: South Americans sporting saber smashed parts of the skull

indicators.note: something smashed is broken apart, so these letters are reordered
sporting means wearing, so one group of letters is worn around another

blocks.note: taken as written in its American spelling, then rearranged
the Incas were the ancient people of Peru

explanation.surface: Peruvians wielding swords crack people's heads.
explanation.walkthrough: Note the container runs the other way from the surface: the scrambled sword wraps around the people.
explanation.definitionFit: The braincase, or cranium, is the section of the skull enclosing the brain.

clue.text: Redhead to deploy trick

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so just that is kept

blocks.note: the head of the word red is its first letter
to deploy is to put to use

explanation.surface: A redhaired person plans to pull a fast one.
explanation.walkthrough: Redhead reads as a ginger-haired person; split, it is the head of 'Red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a deception intended to fool someone, a synonym of trick.

clue.text: Feathers this section of the puzzle

blocks.note: first meaning: the soft fine plumage of birds
second meaning: the half of the clues this one sits in

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at itself: it is one of the vertical clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both soft under-plumage used in pillows and the vertical clue list of a crossword.

clue.text: Leaders of youth are likely enrolled in university

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters, so the first of each is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Young people who lead are probably signed up at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in New Haven, Connecticut, an example of the class.

clue.text: Conviction set us back as I invested in Evita

indicators.note: 'set ... back' is a split phrasal verb: the word it wraps is pushed back to front
completes 'set back', sending the enclosed word in the backward direction
money invested in something goes inside it, so these letters are placed within the next word

blocks.note: Evita was Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president
taken as written, then turned round
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes how being cast as Evita shook their beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set ... back' is split around its object, a common trick. This is the first of several Jane Austen titles in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasion can mean a firmly held belief, as in 'people of every political persuasion', a synonym of conviction.

clue.text: Detective overlooks a knocking sound in the plumbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that overlooks another sits directly on top of it

blocks.note: a PI is a private investigator
ping is the knocking noise of a badly tuned engine

explanation.surface: An investigator ignores a banging noise in the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooks' wants to mean ignores; in a down clue it means sits above.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping is a system of pipes, which is what a building's plumbing consists of.

clue.text: Almost halfway frisky on the subject of word meanings

definitions.text: on the subject of word meanings

indicators.note: almost all of a word means its last letter is left off

blocks.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
antic means playful or capering

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly half-playful about what words mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantic describes anything relating to meaning in language, the study of which is semantics.

clue.text: Front of paddleboat is put in the garage

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the paddle part of the word
the boat half of the compound: Noah's ark is the most famous boat of all

explanation.surface: A paddleboat's bow gets stowed in the garage for winter.
explanation.walkthrough: The compound paddleboat splits into paddle and boat: the front of paddle, then a boat. With 11-across it makes MANSFIELD PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To park a car is to leave it standing somewhere, such as inside a garage.

clue.text: Organ, or part of organ, obscuring terrible din

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are reordered
to obscure something is to cover it up, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: an organ's keyboard is made of keys
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An organ, or one of its keys, drowns out a dreadful racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of organ are the trick: the first is a body part, the second a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney is one of the body's internal organs, filtering waste from the blood.

clue.text: Expunging two diametrically opposed outcomes on a test?

blocks.note: the clue promises two opposite grades: the bottom one first, spelt out as a word
the second outcome is the top grade, read as acing, after the shared letter

explanation.surface: Erasing results that could not be further apart on an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as F-ACING: an F is a failing grade and acing a test means getting an A, two opposite outcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface something is to rub it out or remove all trace of it, a synonym of expunge.

clue.text: Some lions meddled loudly with 22's companion

indicators.note: something said loudly is heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: pried means poked into others' business

explanation.surface: A group of lions noisily interferes alongside a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Pried and PRIDE sound the same. The answer is also the partner of PREJUDICE at 22-across, as in Pride and Prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective noun for a group of lions living together.

clue.text: Author Katherine, in a male domain, precedes 7

blocks.note: a man's, belonging to a male
a field is an area of activity or expertise

explanation.surface: A woman writer finds herself working in a man's world.
explanation.walkthrough: Katherine Mansfield was a New Zealand short-story writer; the answer also comes right before PARK at 7-across, making Austen's Mansfield Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the modernist short-story writer Katherine, and the first word of an Austen novel title.

clue.text: Hawaiian goose takes lick flying around in a V, perhaps

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order
the goose is placed around the other letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: the nene is Hawaii's state bird, a goose
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A Hawaiian goose flies in V formation and gets a licking.
explanation.walkthrough: The V looks like a flock's flight formation, but it is the shape of a garment's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A V-neck is one style of neckline, the edge of a garment around the throat.

clue.text: Raucous Moulin includes the French floor covering

indicators.note: something raucous is wild and disorderly, so these letters are reordered
to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: The rowdy Moulin Rouge in Paris lays down something underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum is a hard-wearing material laid on floors, often in kitchens.

clue.text: Irritate radius and joint

blocks.note: r is the standard symbol for radius
the ankle is the joint between foot and leg

explanation.surface: A broken arm bone and a sore joint are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The radius looks like the forearm bone, alongside a joint, but it is the geometry symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting annoyance or resentment, a synonym of irritate.

clue.text: Harry Potter with inky substance that counteracts supernatural powers

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are pushed out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The boy wizard gets an ink potion that cancels magic.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Potter is the boy wizard, which suits the magic theme, but Harry is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kryptonite is the fictional mineral that strips Superman of his superhuman abilities.

clue.text: Italian road involved in crash of semi

indicators.note: a crash leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so these letters are reordered
something involved in another is caught up inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: An Italian highway is the scene of a truck accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian road' reads as one phrase, a highway; the definition is 'Italian' alone. A semi is a big articulated truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Milanese describes a person or thing from Milan, so it is a kind of Italian.

clue.text: Awareness of family member in the grip of second childhood

indicators.note: something held in the grip of another is clasped inside it

blocks.note: second childhood is an idiom for the decline of old age
sib is short for sibling

explanation.surface: A relative grows aware of a sibling sliding into dotage.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer completes Sense and Sensibility with 25-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensibility is the capacity to perceive and feel, a keen consciousness of things.

clue.text: Men and women quietly elope in a flurry

indicators.note: a flurry is a swirl of agitated movement, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Couples sneak off to marry in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: People are human beings in general, which takes in both men and women.

clue.text: Holy man briefly leaving fish and egg

indicators.note: someone leaving goes away, so those letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: St is the short form of saint
the sturgeon is a large fish, source of caviar

explanation.surface: A monk gives up seafood and eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' looks like food beside the fish, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them on, encouraging them to keep going.

clue.text: Supports illegitimate e-sales

indicators.note: something illegitimate is not properly arranged, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone props up shady online selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Easels are stands that hold up paintings or boards, so they support things.

clue.text: Response to a comedy: kill without scruples at the opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken
going without something means removing it from what remains

blocks.note: to slaughter is to kill in great numbers
the first letter of scruples

explanation.surface: Advice on comedy: an unscrupulous comic goes for the kill at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAUGHTER loses its opening S. Comics talk of killing an audience, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the natural reaction an audience gives to a funny show.

clue.text: Corrupt rep with power to conceal Democratic bias

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoiled and twisted, so these letters are reordered
to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one letter goes within another word

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
juice is slang for power, especially electricity or influence
D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A crooked congressman uses his clout to hide partisan leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep is a US Representative in Congress. The answer partners PRIDE at 10-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice is an unfair preconceived opinion, a synonym of bias.

clue.text: Michael Moore describes a red puppet

indicators.note: to describe can mean to trace around, so these words enclose what is sought

blocks.note: sitting across the two names

explanation.surface: The documentary maker portrays a communist stooge.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'red puppet' in a political film suggests a communist stooge, the sort of figure Michael Moore might depict.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmo is the furry red Muppet on the children's TV show Sesame Street.

clue.text: I can take in premiere of Moonraker in huge movie format

indicators.note: a premiere is a first showing, so only the opening letter is kept
to take in is to receive inside, so one letter goes within the word

blocks.note: taken as written
to can someone is to fire them, which in US slang is to ax them
the first letter of Moonraker

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can watch the opening of a Bond film on a giant screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonraker is a James Bond film, which fits the cinema surface. AX is the American spelling of axe.
explanation.definitionFit: IMAX is a cinema system using very large screens and high-resolution film.

clue.text: I fled from martial arts instructor, feeling connected to 17

indicators.note: someone who has fled from a place is no longer in it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
sensei is the Japanese title for a martial arts teacher

explanation.surface: A student confesses to running away from their karate teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: SENSEI loses its final I. The answer joins SENSIBILITY at 17-across in Sense and Sensibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense is a feeling or perception, and it is linked to 17 by the Austen title.

clue.text: Raised objections in a minimal Wikipedia article

indicators.note: in a down entry, something raised is lifted upward, so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Editors complain about a skimpy online encyclopedia entry.
explanation.definitionFit: On Wikipedia a stub is the label for an article too short to cover its subject.

clue.text: Lazarus returned in the morning with me

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters are read in the backward direction

blocks.note: a.m. means before noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: The biblical Lazarus came back from the dead one morning with the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Lazarus looks like the man raised from the dead, reinforced by 'returned'. He is Emma Lazarus, the poet whose sonnet is on the Statue of Liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the first name of the American poet Lazarus, and also an Austen novel title.

clue.text: A junta seen in disarray by a novelist, most of whose titles appear nearby

definitions.text: a novelist, most of whose titles appear nearby

indicators.note: something in disarray has been thrown out of order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A military junta is viewed in chaos by a writer whose books are close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid holds Persuasion, Pride, Prejudice, Sense, Sensibility, Emma, Mansfield and Park; only Northanger Abbey is missing, hence 'most of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote six major novels, and words from most of their titles fill this grid.
